title: Swapping capslock/ctrl causes false pen actions on Surface Laptop Studio

judgment.rationale: The reporter ties Surface pen symptoms to Keyboard Manager and asks maintainers to reproduce, but the symptom and device/input path are not isolated. Related issue #33968 is described as related but distinct, so it is not a duplicate or confirmed fix.
evidence: The reporter describes false pen actions after swapping CapsLock and Ctrl on a Surface Laptop Studio and says disabling Keyboard Manager removes the symptoms.
The reporter later mentions moving to a Copilot Surface Pro and asks maintainers to reproduce.
Issue #33968 is referenced as related but distinct; it does not establish a shared cause.
judgment.recommended_action: Use a Surface device and a simple CapsLock/Ctrl swap to test whether pen input changes only while Keyboard Manager is active, and capture the exact pen action and hardware state.

fix_assessment.rationale: A remapped modifier event may interact with the Surface pen input stack, but no event trace or controlled reproduction confirms that mechanism.

proposed_fixes.title: Prevent modifier remapping from producing unintended Surface pen actions
proposed_fixes.root_cause: Keyboard Manager's low-level modifier remapping may change an event observed by the Surface pen/input stack in a way that triggers an unintended pen action; this interaction is only a hypothesis.
plan: Reproduce on a Surface Laptop Studio and a Surface Pro with a single CapsLock-to-Ctrl mapping, testing pen input with Keyboard Manager on and off.
Record only the key/pen event sequence and identify whether a synthetic modifier event precedes each false pen action.
If the event trace confirms an interaction, adjust the remap path to preserve the pen input contract and add a regression test for paired key and pen events.
verification: Verify ordinary pen writing, button actions, and modifier remapping work with the mapping both enabled and disabled.
Confirm the false action cannot be reproduced across repeated pen interactions on both supported Surface devices.

confidence.rationale: The reported on/off correlation is meaningful, but the issue does not identify the pen action, device event, or input component involved.

issue_context.summary: A Surface user associates unintended pen actions with a CapsLock/Ctrl swap in Keyboard Manager, but the precise pen gesture and event path are unknown.
known_information: The issue is labeled Issue-Bug, Needs-Repro, Priority-2, and Product-Keyboard Manager.
The reporter says disabling Keyboard Manager removes the pen symptom.
The reporter requests maintainer reproduction and refers to #33968 as related but distinct.
inferences: An interaction between remapped keyboard events and Surface pen input is possible, but the observed temporal association does not establish a root cause.
issue_context.analysis: The reporter's existing request is for reproduction rather than logs. A controlled device-side comparison is more useful than asking the reporter for another bundle; avoid conflating this report with #33968.
initial_investigation: Read the full issue body and all three comments.
Reviewed the Keyboard Manager low-level event handling path; no source evidence directly connects it to the specific Surface pen action.

actions.label: Investigate Surface pen event interaction
actions.note: Implementation design depends on confirming the key/pen event relationship.

actions.label: Compare Surface pen behavior with remapping

reproduce.title: Test Surface pen actions with a CapsLock/Ctrl remap
prerequisites: Surface Laptop Studio or Surface Pro with a working pen.
A clean Keyboard Manager configuration with only CapsLock mapped to Ctrl.
steps: Test a fixed set of pen hover, writing, and button gestures with Keyboard Manager disabled.
Enable Keyboard Manager and the single CapsLock-to-Ctrl mapping; repeat the identical pen gestures.
If an unintended action occurs, record the exact pen gesture and whether a keyboard key was pressed at the same time.
Disable only the mapping and repeat, then compare the result with Keyboard Manager fully disabled.
reproduce.expected_result: Pen behavior remains identical across the controlled states, or a repeatable event sequence identifies the input interaction responsible.
